steps.title: Open Accounts Center on Instagram
steps.desc: Profile → ☰ menu in the top right → "Settings and privacy" → "Accounts Center" at the top.

steps.title: Go to the "Download your information" section
steps.desc: "Your information and permissions" → "Download your information" → "Download information".

steps.title: Select only the follower data
steps.desc: Select your account → "Select some of your information" → check only "Followers and following" from the list. Selecting everything makes the archive take days and hundreds of MB.

steps.title: Set the format to JSON
steps.desc: Date range: "All time". Format: "JSON". Then "Create file". When only follower data is selected, it's usually ready within minutes.

steps.title: Upload the zip file here
steps.desc: Open the .zip file you downloaded with "Choose data archive file". If you've already extracted the zip, you can also select the followers_1.json and following.json files together.

faq.q: Why can't I see who unfollowed me the first time?
faq.a: Instagram never provides "who unfollowed you" info through any method — there's no such record in the archive or in the interface. The only way to find this out is to compare your follower list at two different points in time. The first fetch becomes your starting point; unfollows are listed starting from the second one.

faq.q: Is my password stored in the app?
faq.a: No. The page that opens when you tap "Connect to Instagram" is Instagram's own login page. You enter your password directly into Instagram; the app never sees it, stores it, or sends it anywhere. Only the resulting session cookie stays on your phone.

faq.q: Does live fetching put my account at risk?
faq.a: This method is against Instagram's terms of service. Requests are sent slowly and with delays, but if you repeat it too often, Instagram may impose a temporary "action block" (usually lifts within a few hours). Don't fetch more than once a day; once a week is enough for very large accounts. Use the data archive method if you want zero risk.

faq.q: My account is public, why do I still need to log in?
faq.a: While logged out, you can only see the follower count on a public profile; tapping the list prompts an Instagram login. The endpoints that return the list require a session cookie even on public accounts. This is Instagram's own restriction, not a limitation of the app.

faq.q: What's the difference between the two methods?
faq.a: Live fetching gives instant results; it also brings display names and profile photos, but has no follow date and violates the ToS. The data archive is slow but fully compliant, and includes "since when have I been following this person" info; it has no photos. You can mix both; records accumulate in the same list.

faq.q: Where do the profile photos come from?
faq.a: During a live fetch, Instagram also provides photo addresses, but these addresses are signed and short-lived — they expire after a few days. That's why a photo is downloaded to the phone the first time it appears in a list; after that it's shown even without internet and doesn't disappear from older records. Only what you scroll through gets downloaded, not everything at once. You can turn this off from the History tab, or delete what's already downloaded.
No. Everything happens on your phone. If you delete the app, the records are deleted too.

faq.q: Can I unfollow accounts from the app?
faq.a: No, this was left out on purpose — mass unfollowing is the fastest way to get an account block. Tapping an account in a list opens its profile on Instagram, where you can unfollow manually. You can mark the ones you've dealt with using ✓ to hide them from the list.
